capabilities: Log media positions as one-line entries in a daily note or at the cursor
Auto-merge consecutive sittings into ranges and flag out-of-order jumps with a marker
Render GitHub-style heatmap calendar blocks from logged dogear entries
Mark series complete and list finished titles with start, end, and duration
Customize per-type emoji, labels, inclusive-range defaults, and insert target
disambiguation: Not a web-bookmarking tool; it tracks progress through serial media like books, shows, manga, and podcasts.
extras: Not yet in the community catalog; install via BRAT or manually copying release files. Makes zero network requests. README is written in E-Prime as a deliberate stylistic choice.
intentEvidence: A tracking app owns your data and rings a different bell than the notes you already keep.
motivation: The author wanted a zero-cost record of where you stopped, as a plain line in the note you already write every day, with the work wikilinked, instead of a spreadsheet that dies or a tracking app that owns your data.
problem: Where you stopped in a book, show, or podcast usually lives only in memory, and spreadsheets or tracking apps separate that record from your daily notes.

relations.evidence: install with BRAT pointed at this repo

summary: Media progress tracker that logs one-line dogear entries (books, shows, podcasts, comics) into notes, auto-rolling ranges and flagging sequence breaks.
